newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Five new members join U.N. Security Council.
newsitem.headline: Five new members join U.N. Security Council.

text.p: Costa Rica, Japan, Kenya, Portugal and Sweden on Wednesday officially become members of the powerful 15-member U.N. Security Council for two-year terms.
The council has 10 non-permanent members, five of which rotate each year. The new members replace Botswana, Germany, Italy, Honduras and Indonesia, whose two-year terms expired on Tuesday.
Five other non-permanent members still on the council for another year are: Chile, Egypt, Guinea-Bissau, Poland and South Korea.
In addition the council, which deals with international peace and security, has five permanent members with veto power: the United States, Russia, China, Britain and France.

Japan's ambassador Hisashi Owada takes over the presidency of the council for the month of January from Paolo Fulci of Italy. The council's presidency rotates monthly, according to the English alphabet.
Portugal is expected to take over the council's Iraq sanctions committee, the most active of its sub-groups, diplomats said.
A U.N. working group has been discussing enlarging and reforming the council for nearly three years. But while agreeing the council should be expanded, it has not yet decided how this should be done.

It is widely accepted that, if any new permanent seats are created, two of them should go to Germany and Japan in recognition of their status as economic superpowers and their increasing involvement in such areas as peacekeeping.
